issue_context.title: Improve geo-search: introduction of `_geoBoundingBox`
issue_context.body:
Following this product discussion: https://github.com/meilisearch/product/discussions/431
Specification: https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/223

## API

`_geoBoundingBox([lat, lng], [lat, lng])` using the [`filter` search parameter](https://docs.meilisearch.com/reference/api/search.html#filter)

`[lat, lng]` <- Top left corner,
`[lat, lng]` <- Bottom right corner

## Implementation

- [x] Implement changes
- [X] Create the spec about name and behavior changes -> https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/223

## Impacted teams

Pinging @meilisearch/docs-team, also @meilisearch/integration-team even if I'm not sure. Feel free to unsubscribe from this issue if I was wrong to ping you.

---

<s>Pinging @mlemesle since I think you are interested in implementing this 😄 </s>
This issue is opened to anyone!

Feel free to ask any questions to implement this issue. The core team is available to guide you through this contribution, even if it's your first one.
We recommend referring to the [CONTRIBUTING.md guidelines](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), especially if it's your first contribution to this repository.
Thanks in advance for your involvement ❤️

review_comments: I propagated the change to the original `parse<T>` function that replace span by value() here. This feels like a bug fix indeed, but I am uncertain of its impact. Can you give me some insight as to why this was changed?

The reason for this change is that we need to create « fake token » that has no span for the bounding box.

If you ask for the point between (170, 0) and (-170, 0) we need to generate the following filters: `(_geo.lnt 170 TO 180 AND _geo.lnt -180 TO -170) AND (handle _geo.lat)`

Our issue is that in the filter `_geoRadius((170, 0), (-170, 0))`, the token `180` doesn't appear anywhere and thus doesn't have a span in the source filter.
The trick is to create a token that has a span that points to `_geoRadius` but contains the value `180`/`-180`.

> This feels like a bug fix indeed

Actually, no, because until now, the only case where we could have a difference between the `value()` and the `span` was on strings with escaped characters.
Thanks for the explanation ☺️ Is this documented somewhere in the code? If not, I feel like it possibly ought to?
I added a clear explanation (I think) about the implementation of the geoboundingbox + simplified a little bit the usage of the `Token`.
